The operating system turns the assembled hardware into a computer you can use. In this stage, confirm the target drive, test the live system, install Linux Mint, create the classroom account, and verify that the hardware works after restart.

## Use the canonical guide

[Open **Install Linux Mint 22.3 Xfce**](../linux-operating-systems/install-linux-mint.qmd).

That page contains the current step-by-step installation choices, screenshots, checks, and lab log. It is the only installation procedure maintained on this site.

## Computer Systems evidence

Add these items to your activity package:

- the assigned computer and target drive
- confirmation that the live session recognized the display, keyboard, mouse, network, sound, USB, and storage
- the installed operating-system version
- the computer name and account check
- one post-install update or configuration step
- one problem you found and how you tested it

After installation, continue with [Terminal Basics](../linux-operating-systems/terminal-basics.qmd), then return to [CS07: RAM upgrade](cs07-ram-upgrade.qmd).
